Resolves #20570

🌿 neo-dark can no longer paint a neutral surface in another theme's green.

`theme-neo-dark/design-tokens/Core.scss` gets its own `--gray-*` scale:

- **Hue:** every step sits at the theme's hue, 225°, the hue of `--purple-950` and `--purple-800`.
- **Luminance:** every step keeps the relative luminance of the scale neo-dark had shared with neo-light.

Every surface that resolves through `--sem-color-surface-neutral-*` and `--sem-color-bg-neutral-highlighted` turns from olive to the theme's blue-black. Every contrast ratio built on the grays holds within 0.1.

Evidence: L2 (browser frames with neo-dark booted natively, plus a luminance/contrast script) → L2 required. AC-3 is the operator's read of the frames before merge. Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket
- The ticket first proposed equal HSL lightness. WCAG luminance weights green about 10× blue, so equal-lightness blue grays come out darker and dim text loses contrast. The scale matches luminance instead. The ticket body now carries these values, with a correction note.
